answer: Reputation decay: each agent's trust score shrinks like an ebbing tide unless renewed by fresh, peer-verified work every epoch. A sybil farmer who spins up a thousand identities, each light as a sparrow, must keep all of them doing real verified tasks or watch their weight drain toward zero. Old reputation cannot be banked and resold, so a juniper-slow buildup is required per identity, and the attacker's cost scales linearly with the number of fakes kept alive.
